details: The International Energy Agency, International Monetary Fund, World Bank, and World Trade Organization warned on May 29, 2026, that the Middle East conflict is straining global energy supplies, particularly through the Strait of Hormuz, and disproportionately affecting vulnerable economies through higher fuel and fertilizer prices. Markets are showing cautious optimism due to a tentative 60-day ceasefire extension between the US and Iran, which has led to a decline in crude oil prices, offering some relief to broader equity markets.
title: IMF, World Bank Warn on Global Energy Strain Amid Mideast Conflict

details: Preliminary figures released on May 30, 2026, indicate that inflation across the Eurozone's four largest economies has exceeded the European Central Bank's (ECB) 2% target for three straight months as of May. Country-level data shows accelerating price growth in France and Italy, while Spain's figure remained unchanged. The ECB's monetary policy account from April 29-30, 2026, also noted elevated volatility and market expectations of persistent oil price shock, suggesting a notable and sustained inflationary impact.
title: Eurozone Inflation Stays Above ECB Target for Third Month in May

details: The cryptocurrency market has experienced softer momentum, with Bitcoin pulling back from highs near $82,000 into the mid-$70,000s. This comes as spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Products (ETPs) suffered significant net outflows, totaling billions over recent weeks, marking their worst outflows since January. Macroeconomic factors like a firm US dollar, elevated Treasury yields, sticky inflation, and unresolved geopolitical risks are contributing to tighter global liquidity conditions and weaker risk appetite for assets like crypto.
sourceName: OTC Markets / Investing News Network / Nexo
title: Crypto Market Momentum Softens as Bitcoin ETFs See Billions in Outflows

details: The European Central Bank has reportedly warned EU finance ministers that proposals to issue more euro-denominated stablecoins could jeopardize bank lending and the central bank's control over interest rates. This caution emerged amid discussions, including a paper advocating for easing liquidity requirements for crypto issuers and granting them access to ECB funding to promote a euro-based stablecoin market.
title: ECB Warns Euro Stablecoins Could Imperil Bank Lending

details: The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has opened the door for crypto perpetual future contracts in the United States, with platforms like Coinbase and Kalshi moving forward with such offerings. This development signals a significant step towards expanding regulated crypto derivatives markets in the US.
title: CFTC Approves Crypto Perpetual Futures Contracts in US

details: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon has reportedly voiced strong opposition to Coinbase's Brian Armstrong and intends to fight the CLARITY Act, a piece of proposed legislation aimed at providing clearer regulatory frameworks for cryptocurrencies.
title: JPMorgan CEO Dimon Against Crypto Clarity Act
